claims.claim: Four weighted-square inequalities are necessary and sufficient for strong substitutes for binary E,A,B under quadratic scoring, with arbitrary support.
Two inequalities classify the direction garbling a binary source and adding an arbitrary finite second signal for square-integrable real targets.
checks: finite vector-target audit: 105 cases, 1,785 direct scores, 90 failure witnesses

claims.claim: A failed rational-input substitutes test produces a finite rational two-report negative-gap witness.
Equality conditions and quantitative disclosure-gap bounds follow from the exact nonnegative decomposition.
limits: Operational retained-source-uncertainty strictness, not syntactic strict-lattice terminology

claims.claim: For independent nondegenerate binary sources, strong substitutes iff the posterior has zero interaction.
For full signal support and additive posterior kappa+uA+vB, strong substitutes iff u*v*Cov(A,B)>=0.
A full-support weak/moderate-substitutes model with whole margin 1/1024 has an explicit disclosure gap -11/10240.
Strong complements in the same binary model admit two endpoint tests and at most one quadratic-vertex test in each direction.
checks: independent cross-check of 3,616 returned complement failures

claims.claim: An equivalent endpoint criterion was not found in the recorded bounded prior-art search.
limits: No exhaustive paid bibliographic database or author enquiry

claims.claim: Strong substitutes imply projective substitutes in this binary quadratic model, strictly; the displayed rational separator passes all 32 projective comparisons.
limits: Reviewer-derived addition; not universal scoring-rule equivalence.
